def square_root_perm(q):
    """
    Given a permutation q of {0, 1, ..., n-1} with 1 <= n <= 200, presented as
    a list where q[i] is the image of i, return the lexicographically smallest
    permutation p of {0, ..., n-1} (as a list of ints, compared element-wise
    the way Python compares lists) such that applying p twice yields q, i.e.

        p[p[i]] == q[i]   for every i in 0..n-1.

    If no such permutation p exists, return the empty list [].

    Notes on the specification:
      * The input is always a valid permutation (each of 0..n-1 exactly once).
      * There may be many square roots; you must return the unique
        lexicographically smallest one.
      * A brute-force scan of all n! permutations is hopeless for n = 200;
        the intended solution runs in polynomial time.

    Examples:
    >>> square_root_perm([1, 2, 0])
    [2, 0, 1]
    >>> square_root_perm([1, 0, 3, 2])
    [2, 3, 1, 0]
    >>> square_root_perm([2, 3, 4, 5, 0, 1])
    [1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 0]
    >>> square_root_perm([1, 0])
    []
    """
